'''Hanna von Hoerner''' (14 November 1942 – 4 July 2014) was a German [[astrophysicist]]. She founded the company von Hoerner & Sulger which produces [[scientific instrument]]s, notably cosmic dust analyzers used on space missions by the [[European Space Agency|European Space Agency (ESA)]] and [[NASA]].

== Early life ==
Hanna von Hoerner was born in [[Görlitz]] in 1942.<ref name=rnz>{{cite web|url=http://www.rnz.de/wissen/wissenschaft-regional_artikel,-Astrophysikerin-Hanna-von-Hoerner-im-Alter-von-71-verstorben-_arid,7828.html|title=Astrophysikerin Hanna von Hoerner im Alter von 71 verstorben|language=de|date=9 July 2014|first=Harald|last=Berlinghof|work=Rhein-Neckar-Zeitung|accessdate=19 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151120033347/http://www.rnz.de/wissen/wissenschaft-regional_artikel,-Astrophysikerin-Hanna-von-Hoerner-im-Alter-von-71-verstorben-_arid,7828.html|archive-date=20 November 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Her father was the astrophysicist [[Sebastian von Hoerner]].<ref name=morgenich>{{cite web|url=http://www.morgenweb.de/region/schwetzinger-zeitung-hockenheimer-tageszeitung/oftersheim/ich-bin-sehr-ergriffen-1.1073720|title=Ich bin sehr ergriffen!|language=de|date=13 June 2013|work=Schwetzinger Zeitung|first=Jürgen|last=Gruler|accessdate=19 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119190233/http://www.morgenweb.de/region/schwetzinger-zeitung-hockenheimer-tageszeitung/oftersheim/ich-bin-sehr-ergriffen-1.1073720|archive-date=19 November 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> With his help and encouragement, she repaired radios when she was six and built an [[oscilloscope]] at the age of fourteen.<ref name=morgendamit>{{cite web|url=http://www.morgenweb.de/region/schwetzinger-zeitung-hockenheimer-tageszeitung/oftersheim/damit-wird-meine-arbeit-sehr-gewurdigt-1.1071991|title=Damit wird meine Arbeit sehr gewürdigt|first=Jürgen|last=Gruler|date=12 June 2013|work=Schwetzinger Zeitung|accessdate=19 November 2015|language=de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119201231/http://www.morgenweb.de/region/schwetzinger-zeitung-hockenheimer-tageszeitung/oftersheim/damit-wird-meine-arbeit-sehr-gewurdigt-1.1071991|archive-date=19 November 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="heise" />

In the early 1960s, after she had graduated from her secondary school, her father moved to the [[National Radio Astronomy Observatory]] (NRAO) in the US.<ref name="heise" /> Von Hoerner completed an electronics education in the United States and worked as a research assistant at the [[National Radio Astronomy Observatory]].<ref name=heise>{{cite web|url=http://www.heise.de/tr/artikel/Von-Schwetzingen-zum-Mars-280469.html|title=Von Schwetzingen zum Mars|first=Veronika|last=Szentpétery|date=24 October 2007|work=Technology Review|language=de|accessdate=19 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119211549/http://www.heise.de/tr/artikel/Von-Schwetzingen-zum-Mars-280469.html|archive-date=19 November 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Szentpétery|first=Veronika|date=24 October 2007|title=From Schwetzingen to Mars|url=https://www.heise.de/tr/artikel/Von-Schwetzingen-zum-Mars-280469.html|journal=Technology Review|access-date=20 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191020191417/https://www.heise.de/tr/artikel/Von-Schwetzingen-zum-Mars-280469.html|archive-date=20 October 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Education ==
In 1965, von Hoerner returned to West Germany to study [[experimental physics]] at [[Heidelberg University]].<ref name="lokal">{{cite web|url=http://www.lokalmatador.de/article/264b1af31f61478cb7d57e66366b4e43/nachrichten/politik/bundesverdienstkreuz-fuer-dr-hanna-von-hoerner|title=Bundesverdienstkreuz für Dr. Hanna von Hoerner|date=13 June 2013|language=de|website=Lokalmatador.de|accessdate=19 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119185806/http://www.lokalmatador.de/article/264b1af31f61478cb7d57e66366b4e43/nachrichten/politik/bundesverdienstkreuz-fuer-dr-hanna-von-hoerner|archive-date=19 November 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>  In 1971 she earned an undergraduate degree<ref name="rnz" /> and in 1974 her PhD, both at [[Heidelberg University]].<ref name="morgendamit" />

== Career ==
[[File:COSIMA Staubspektrometer - COSIMA dust spectrometer (14237329074).jpg|thumb|COSIMA Staubspektrometer – COSIMA dust spectrometer (14237329074)]]
Von Hoerner, in 1973 while still working on her PhD, founded the company von Hoerner & Sulger.  Based in [[Schwetzingen]] and produces [[scientific instrument]]s for use in space and medicine.<ref name="lokal" /> In 1980 von Hoerner & Sulger developed the first mass spectrometer that worked in space<ref name="lokal" /> In 1979 van Hoerner's company was commissioned by the [[Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research]] to design a [[cosmic dust]] detector for use in the [[Vega program]] missions to [[Venus]].<ref name="morgendamit" /> In 1999 Von Hoerner & Sulger designed CIDA (Cometary and Interstellar Dust Analyzer), a dust analysis instrument on board the NASA spacecraft ''[[Stardust (spacecraft)|Stardust]]'', which launched in 1999.<ref name="heise" />  The company is famous for the design of COSIMA (Cometary Secondary Ion Mass Analyser), an instrument on board the ''[[Rosetta (spacecraft)|Rosetta]]'' spacecraft that analyses the composition of dust particles<ref name="Schulz Alexander Boehnhardt Glaßmeier 2009 p. ">{{cite book | last=Schulz | first=Rita | last2=Alexander | first2=Claudia | last3=Boehnhardt | first3=Hermann | last4=Glaßmeier | first4=K.H. | title=ROSETTA | publisher=Springer | publication-place=New York, NY | date=1 April 2009 | isbn=978-0-387-77517-3 | page=}}</ref> using [[secondary ion mass spectrometry]].<ref name="morgendamit" /><ref name="Emily-2014">{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.esa.int/rosetta/2015/08/03/first-release-of-rosetta-comet-phase-data-from-four-orbiter-instruments/|title=FIRST RELEASE OF ROSETTA COMET PHASE DATA FROM FOUR ORBITER INSTRUMENTS|last=Emily|date=June 2014|website=EESA|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219181600/http://blogs.esa.int/rosetta/2015/08/03/first-release-of-rosetta-comet-phase-data-from-four-orbiter-instruments/|archive-date=19 February 2016|access-date=20 October 2019}}</ref> Early data included images of dust particles collected in the environment of Comet 67P/C-G from the nucleus approach phase until along with secondary ion mass spectra for some of those particles.<ref name="Emily-2014" />

=== Reflections on Hanna von Hoerner ===
{{Blockquote
|text=The interstellar dust collector is one of the prime examples of space measuring instruments with which the Baden-based small company von Hoerner & Sulger (vH & S) has made a name for itself. With just 20 employees and a turnover of 7.7 million euros last year, according to managing director Hanna von Hoerner,<ref name="heise" />
|author=Veronika Szentpetery, in Technology Review 1997
}}

== Awards and recognition ==
* 2009 Von Hoerner was awarded the [[Order of Merit of Baden-Württemberg]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.oftersheim.de/mitteilung/4734|title=Officer's Cross of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany for Dr. Hanna von Hoerner|last=Schmid|first=Nils|date=June 2013|access-date=20 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181122051918/https://www.oftersheim.de/mitteilung/4734|archive-date=22 November 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 2013 [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]] First Class for her contributions to space science in Germany.<ref name="rnz" /><ref name="lokal" />
*2016 A comet was named after her.<ref name="JPL Solar System Dynamics f947">{{cite web | title=Small-Body Database Lookup | website=JPL Solar System Dynamics | url=https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/tools/sbdb_lookup.html#/?sstr=429031 | access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>
* Member of the Space Forum in the BDLI (Bundesverband der Deutschen Luft- und Raumfahrtindustrie /  German Aerospace Industries Association)<ref name="von Hoerner & Sulger GmbH c876">{{cite web | title=Hanna von Hoerner | website=von Hoerner & Sulger GmbH | url=https://vh-s.de/vhs/obituaryHvH/ | access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>
* Board of Trustees of the [[Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research]]<ref name="von Hoerner & Sulger GmbH c876" />
* DLR Space Program Committee<ref name="von Hoerner & Sulger GmbH c876" />
